newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities prices rise.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities prices rise.

text.p: Singapore government securities trade closed higher in an improved market on interbank and retail interest, dealers said.
"The market has improved mainly because of shorter terms in interbank rates. Bonds also closed at higher term rates," said a local dealer.
In treasury bills, three-months increased at 2.88/2.83 percent compared to Wednesday's 2.83/2.78 percent and one-year closed at 2.73/2.68 percent against the previous 2.72/2.67 percent.

Among bonds, April 1999 eased at S$98.50/98.60 compared with Wednesday's S$98.55/98.60, September 2001 increased to S$96.45/96.55 from the previous S$96.40/96.50 while June 2003 closed at S$94.23/94.33 from S$94.23/94.28.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased 1-1/2 points to 2-5/8 2-1/2 percent versus Wednesday's 3-1/8 3 percent.
